title: Chreode: A Cell World Model for One-Step Temporal Dynamics and Perturbation Prediction
evidence_anchors: Abstract and pp. 2-7; Tables 1-4 pp. 8-9; Scope pp. 9-10; Appendices A-C pp. 12-16; ablations pp. 17-18; NeurIPS checklist pp. 19-25
reviewer_notes: Highest claim is action-conditioned because the paper defines a nominal intervention-conditioned transition and perturbation task. However, the action token is null during temporal pretraining and the Norman result replaces a GEARS embedding rather than evaluating a standalone action-conditioned Chreode operator. Multiple elapsed-time targets are one-step queries, not free-running rollout. Cross-dataset results use fine-tuning, so external evidence is adapted rather than frozen. The do(a) notation triggers causal scrutiny, but no effect contrast, identification strategy, overlap analysis, or counterfactual validation is provided. Qualitative dual-use discussion supports safety=1 without a hazard test.

title: Clin-JEPA: A Multi-Phase Co-Training Framework for Joint-Embedding Predictive Pretraining on EHR Patient Trajectories
evidence_anchors: Fig. 1 and Secs. 3-4 pp. 3-6; Fig. 2 and Sec. 5.2 pp. 6-7; Fig. 3 pp. 8-9; Fig. 4 and Sec. 5.4 p. 9; Appendices A-D pp. 13-18
reviewer_notes: The model genuinely consumes its own predicted latent states in a 48-hour autoregressive rollout, with horizon-resolved L1 drift and collapse diagnostics. Actions are encoded, but their contribution is never isolated by an action-agnostic comparator or perturbation. All evidence is from MIMIC-IV, and downstream utility is an offline risk-probe result rather than clinician or policy evaluation. The paper makes no counterfactual or treatment-effect claim, so causal fields are NA. Public code plus detailed data construction and hyperparameters support reproducibility=2 despite credentialed MIMIC access.

title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories
evidence_anchors: Main text pp. 1-7, especially Secs. 3.1-3.4 and 4.2-4.4; Tables 1-4 pp. 6-7; Appendices B-C pp. 10-20; changed-path and first-divergence analyses pp. 21-24; rollout diagnostics pp. 25-27; eICU protocol pp. 27-34
reviewer_notes: The recursive correction path consumes its prior latent state and is evaluated within a 48-hour hybrid forecast, with lead-wise trajectory and discrepancy diagnostics. Action evidence is strong because no-action comparators, donor-path replacement, timing/response ablations, and divergence alignment are reported. The eICU study is independently retrained and all hospitals overlap training, so it is adapted cross-database evidence rather than frozen validation. The authors explicitly disclaim causal effects and keep outcomes fixed during path replacement; causal fields are therefore NA, not positive evidence. Code is promised only upon publication.

title: Model-based reinforcement learning for ultrasound-driven autonomous microrobots.
evidence_anchors: Main article Figs. 1-6 and pp. 1076-1085; Methods pp. 1085-1088; Data and Code Availability p. 1088; Extended Data Figs. 1-4; Supplementary Notes S3, S5, S9-S11 and Figs. 11-16
reviewer_notes: Planning is supported because latent imagined trajectories train a sequential policy that executes real ultrasound commands in closed-loop image feedback. Direct state-transition fidelity and horizon-resolved imagined-rollout error are not evaluated, so state, dynamics, and rollout remain indirect/limited. Action settings and magnitudes are varied, but there is no action-agnostic comparator. Sim-to-real and unseen-channel results require continued adaptation, not frozen validation. Physical hazard evidence is unusually strong for this corpus: collision, overshoot, flow displacement, tracking loss, cavitation concern, constraints, shutdown, reset, and action-reversal rescue are tested or demonstrated. Public code, data, and checkpoints support reproducibility=2.

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
evidence_anchors: Secs. 1-2 pp. 2-6; Fig. 1 p. 4; Sec. 3 pp. 6-8 and Table 1 p. 8; Fig. 2 and conclusion pp. 8-9
reviewer_notes: The title and framing claim relevance to surgical motion planning, so coding is against planning. The experiment nevertheless forecasts the recorded expert trajectory as an output and never conditions on, selects, optimizes, or executes a chosen action. It earns direct state/dynamics and free-running rollout evidence because decoded visual states and trajectory errors are reported across five segments of a fully autoregressive 15-step rollout. Decision evidence is only an offline planning proxy. The single benchmark, missing split details, no repeated-run statistics, absent uncertainty, and lack of public training code limit external and reproducibility evidence.
